task: Write one sentence of your own using the word abstruse. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know abstruse should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Halfway through the seminar on knot theory, Priya realized the proofs had grown too abstruse for anyone without a decade of training.
A challenging article makes you work but rewards ordinary effort; it stops short of abstruse, which demands training most readers simply don't have.
Impenetrable goes further than abstruse — an abstruse proof yields to the right specialist, while an impenetrable one lets nobody in at all.

Recondite matter is deep and known mainly to specialists, because so few people ever study it; like abstruse, it locates the difficulty in the material's depth. Neither word implies a gatekeeper — a recondite treatise is open to anyone willing to put in the years.

Esoteric material is meant for a small inner circle, restricted on purpose so that only insiders can read it. Abstruse is different: abstruse ideas are open to anyone, but they run so deep that ordinary preparation isn't enough. Esoteric guards a door; abstruse simply towers.
